plan_a_advantages: More targeted hill training for trail-specific strength.
Longer runs with significant elevation gain to build endurance.
A greater variety of workout types (long, hills, easy) to stimulate different physiological adaptations.
plan_b_advantages: Prioritizes recovery with more rest days.
Includes a dedicated strength and mobility session, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall running efficiency.
reasoning: Plan A is better suited for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more structured hill work (8 x 400m repeats) and longer runs (40km) with elevation gain, directly addressing the demands of trail running and building the necessary strength and endurance. Plan B, while including longer runs, focuses heavily on easy, sustained efforts and a single tempo session, which may not provide the targeted stimulus needed for speed development. Plan A’s varied workout types and emphasis on uphill strength will be more effective for improving trail running performance.
